<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>9</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(3x)^{-2} = \frac{1}{9x^2}</annotation></semantics></math>: the exponent would apply to the 3 as well.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>16</mn><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16^{-3/4}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mn>16</mn><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{16^{3/4}}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mroot><mn>16</mn><mn>4</mn></mroot><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{\left(\sqrt[4]{16}\right)^3}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{2^3}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{8}</annotation></semantics></math>.

Power of a power multiplies: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>6</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x^3)^2 = x^6</annotation></semantics></math>. A negative exponent on the whole base <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2x)</annotation></semantics></math> is one over <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2x)^3</annotation></semantics></math>: equal.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>8</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{8} \cdot \frac{1}{x^3} = \frac{1}{8x^3}</annotation></semantics></math>: equal.

why.correct: Same base, multiplied: add the exponents. <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3} = \frac{3}{6} + \frac{2}{6} = \frac{5}{6}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}</annotation></semantics></math> is undefined where <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos x = 0</annotation></semantics></math>, as at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. The log of a power: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\ln 2 = \ln 2^3 = \ln 8</annotation></semantics></math>. Log of a quotient, then log of a power: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln x^3 - \ln y = 3\ln x - \ln y</annotation></semantics></math>.

The log of a quotient is a difference of logs, not a quotient of logs.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln(x^3) = 3\ln x</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln(3x)</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln(x^3) = 3\ln x</annotation></semantics></math>; <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\ln x)^3</annotation></semantics></math> is something else.

Exponentiate both sides: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x + 2 = e^1 = e</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>≈</mo><mn>0.718</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = e - 2 \approx 0.718</annotation></semantics></math>. A logarithm needs a positive input: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4 - x > 0</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo><</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x < 4</annotation></semantics></math>.

For <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x > 4</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4 - x</annotation></semantics></math> is negative.

The input of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4 - x</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>.
